questions.question: What does the idiom "barking up the wrong tree" mean?

options.text: Something good that isn't recognized at first.
Being upset for something that happened in the past.
Having something that is certain is much better than taking a risk for more, because chances are you might lose everything.
Pursuing the wrong course of action or making a mistaken assumption

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"barking up the wrong tree"** means:

 
 
• Pursuing the wrong course of action or making a mistaken assumption (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना या गलत धारणा बनाना)
 
 
 
• **Example:** If you think John will help you, you're** barking up the wrong tree**; he has never been reliable.
 
• **Explanation:** The idiom suggests that a person is directing their efforts towards the wrong goal or making an incorrect assumption. (यह मुहावरा बताता है कि कोई व्यक्ति गलत लक्ष्य की ओर अपने प्रयासों को निर्देशित कर रहा है या गलत धारणा बना रहा है।)
 
• **Example:** She kept asking her brother for advice on her career, but she was barking up the wrong tree; he had no experience in her field.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Something good that isn't recognized at first** (पहले नहीं पहचाना गया कुछ अच्छा)

 
 
• **Example:** The new employee was like a diamond in the rough; her talents weren't recognized at first.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Being upset for something that happened in the past** (भूतकाल में हुई किसी बात के लिए परेशान होना)
 
 
• **Example:** He couldn't move on with his life because he was still upset about things that happened years ago.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Having something that is certain is much better than taking a risk for more, because chances are you might lose everything** (कुछ निश्चित होना और अधिक के लिए जोखिम लेने से बेहतर है, क्योंकि संभावना है कि आप सब कुछ खो सकते हैं)
 
 
• **Example:** He decided to accept the job offer rather than wait for a better one, as he believed a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank(4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**yet**" is used to introduce a contrast or a contradiction to the preceding statement.
 
• In the given context,** "yet"** highlights that despite the recognition of privacy as a fundamental right, the government's personal data protection bill is still lacking in some aspects.
 
• The other options: "**So**" (indicating consequence), "**Such**" (used for emphasis), and "**Through**" (indicating movement) do not fit the intended meaning.

**Complete Sentence:** *The Supreme Court in India has recognised privacy as a fundamental right. Yet__ the government's personal data protection bill introduced in Parliament leaves much to be desired.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **So**: Indicates a cause and effect relationship which doesn't fit here as well as "yet."
 
• **Such**: Used for emphasis, but doesn't introduce a contradiction effectively.
 
• **Through**: Indicates movement or a means of doing something, which doesn’t fit the context of the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank(5)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**a lot**" is used to indicate that something is lacking significantly.
 
• In the given context,** "leaves a lot to be desired"** means the government's personal data protection bill is considerably inadequate.
 
• The other options: "**might**" (indicating possibility), "**very**" (used as an adverb for emphasis without qualification), and "**so**" (denoting extent or manner) do not convey the intended meaning effectively.

**Complete Sentence:** *The Supreme Court in India has recognised privacy as a fundamental right. Yet the government's personal data protection bill introduced in Parliament leaves a lot__ to be desired.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **A lot**: Indicates a significant amount and** fits the context** of something being considerably lacking.
 
• **Might**: Indicates possibility, but does not fit the context here.
 
• **Very**: Used as an adverb for emphasis, but does not indicate the extent of inadequacy.
 
• **So**: Used to denote extent or manner, but does not fit the context of inadequacy properly.
